name: addpipe24_cla_block4
rationale: Prior attempts show WNS is the dominant reward term and hand-built full-width prefix trees (Kogge-Stone/Sklansky) either match baseline delay at higher area or cut area but lose ~0.08ns of WNS, apparently due to wide-fanout combine signals feeding many bits. This candidate uses a classic two-level carry-lookahead structure: 6 blocks of 4 bits each compute local generate/propagate (2-level SOP), block-level carries are obtained directly via a parallel sum-of-products formula across only 6 terms (not a 24-wide prefix tree, avoiding the large per-bit combine-cell count of KS/Sklansky), and each bit's final carry is resolved locally from its block carry-in plus 2 more logic levels. This keeps logical depth comparable to the prefix-tree adders (~5-6 levels) while sharply cutting the total number of combine cells (since only 6 block-level nodes need wide combining instead of 24 bit-level nodes), aiming to land at lower area than both KS (549.8) and baseline (530.9) while preserving WNS closer to baseline than the Sklansky attempt did.
